reader_summary: I can now explain both the debugging procedure and the metric directly from the lesson. The assistant may answer badly because ASR changes the question or because chat fails even with the correct words. Feeding a correct transcript directly to the chat stage gives a comparison route; feeding the original ASR transcript gives the full voice route. Both use matching context, photo and weights. In the dinner example the missing 不 removes the non-spicy condition. CER is the minimum number of character insertions, deletions or replacements needed to restore the original words, divided by the original character count. Inserting 不 is one edit, and the original has nine characters including its full stop, so the percentage is 1/9 × 100 ≈ 11.1. The function returns those quantities in a dictionary; the last comparison is False. Restoring 不 gives zero edits, zero CER and True, yet a correct transcript alone does not guarantee a helpful answer that follows the request. The section also explains why original ASR output should remain in evaluation records and why read-aloud questions leave spontaneous speech and difficult audio conditions untested. I found no remaining readability obstacle in the current assigned section.
